scope: Static source/claim/media wording and conservative source-family allocations. No human approval, field visit, specialist endorsement, build, rendered-browser or live publication verification claimed.

corrections_resolved.finding: Guptaganga sentence had named disappearance/re-emergence as though the name referred to an event.
corrections_resolved.resolution: Corrected to river disappearing underground and re-emerging at Brahma Kunda, then called Guptaganga. The preceding sacred-account attribution remains explicit.

corrections_resolved.finding: Original report title used Environment, not Environmental.
corrections_resolved.resolution: Public Kanjhari report note now follows original title. Original date October2020 retained, not2022 upload date.

claim_checks.basis: Direct original district body describes hills/valleys and Brahmeswar Mahadev beside Baitarani. No new construction chronology or unsupported mountain height/rank introduced.

Original links Brahma, cow-nostril imagery, underground/re-emergent flow and Brahma Kunda/Guptaganga. Final prose explicitly calls this the district sacred account; no literal divine foundation or proven geological mechanism is asserted.
Direct original Baruni section supports shrine pilgrimage and Brahma Kunda ritual bathing. No current festival date, crowd estimate or bathing-safety promise.
Annual Report2020–21 printed17/PDF28 directly and visually inspected: Baitarani rises at Gonasika and reaches Bay of Bengal. No disputed total length or source altitude used.

Kanjhari report printed15/PDF18 directly and visually inspected: north toward Jharkhand border, then east toward Anandapur subdivision/Bhadrak. Draft preserves broad direction without inventing an itinerary or intermediate distance.

District transport sections establish Kendujhar as approach town. Contradictory30/40km numbers and obsolete only-airport statement omitted. Checking onward access and asking before ritual photographs are editorial advice, not operational or legal claims.

source_access.method: Reuse of actual bounded original readings from this task; no redundant new search. District temple/culture bodies directly read through web open. Both original DoWR PDFs downloaded and title/relevant pages rendered and visually inspected. Exact URLs, hashes, publication dates and limits in source-manifest.json.

limits: Not an inspection of every page in either report.

word_budget.method: Whitespace tokens after removing Markdown URLs, heading markers and reference IDs; hyphenated words and initials count as single tokens. Each distinct authored field counted; identical imported reuse across cards/discovery/sharing is not treated as a fresh source allowance. All31 metadata words charged to both textual families and, additionally, photo family. All12 headings charged to each textual family.

families.family: Kendujhar district, temple plus culture pages
Odisha Water Resources, annual report plus Kanjhari report and any related state river-geography reuse
Commons photo and retained creator description

word_budget.inclusions: Photo-specific visual description and creator location are supported by the actual image/source, not borrowed district flora or temple claims. Full caption is additionally charged to district as a conservative overlap. Image title and preview_credit are charged even where renderer visibility may vary. Existing separate-destination reading cards and generic navigation/contribution boilerplate introduce no source-derived Gonasika facts. Internal provenance/dimensions/hashes are not public prose.
word_budget.originality: No copied expressive narrative or extended quotation found. Factual names, dates, soil-free geography terms and bibliographic titles do not approach25words of expressive quotation per family. No tourism-blog or Antaranga prose imported.

media_review.method: Personally viewed actual public1280×960 JPEG and read relevant identity/date/credit/licence passages in root-retained original Commons HTML. Separate Drishti acquisition/delivery review remains separately attributable.
